why_how.text: Iowa move-over law orders a lane change past any stopped rig flashing its lights, from emergency, tow, recovery, maintenance, construction, and waste or recycling trucks down to an ordinary car blinking its hazards.
Where shifting lanes is impossible, illegal, or unsafe, slow to a reasonable and proper pace for conditions and stand ready to halt.
Breaking the move-over law can suspend your license for up to one year.
Flashing stopped rigs demand a lane change first, while an impossible shift drops you to a slow, stop-ready crawl.
Tow and work rigs with flashers trigger move-over, and so does an ordinary car blinking its hazards.

When a lane change cannot be made, is illegal or would be unsafe, slow to a speed that is reasonable for existing conditions and prepare to stop. A violation may lead to a license suspension lasting as long as one year.
After a crash with nobody hurt, Iowa law makes you steer an operable car that can move safely out of the travel lanes.
Every minute a blocked interstate lane lingers, the chance of a second crash climbs by roughly two point eight percent.
Operable cars must clear the lanes after a no-injury crash, because each blocked minute lifts secondary-crash odds by roughly two point eight percent.
